pr_title: [Merged by Bors] - Improve change detection behavior for transform propagation
pr_body:
# Objective
Fix #4647. If any child is changed, or even reordered, `Changed<Children>` is true, which causes transform propagation to propagate changes to all siblings of a changed child, even if they don't need to be.

## Solution
As `Parent` and `Children` are updated in tandem in hierarchy commands after #4800. `Changed<Parent>` is true on the child when `Changed<Children>` is true on the parent. However, unlike checking children, checking `Changed<Parent>` is only localized to the current entity and will not force propagation to the siblings.

Also took the opportunity to change propagation to use `Query::iter_many` instead of repeated `Query::get` calls. Should cut a bit of the overhead out of propagation. This means we won't panic when there isn't a `Parent` on the child, just skip over it.

The tests from #4608 still pass, so the change detection here still works just fine under this approach.
pr_comments: Neat! Do we have any benchmarks for this? I'd love to see the impact of this change in a large scene, with varying percentages of the entities moving.
`many_foxes` is a poor benchmark for this since all of the transforms change. There is the transform propagation stress test which covers a few nice ranges. I'll test against that soon.
Ah perfect, that's exactly what I was hoping for: I just didn't remember if we'd merged it.
On second thought, we actually don't have anything to test the case where we're reparenting transforms, only those that mutate `Transform`. Not sure how to better test this.

Hmm. It's good to check those still for regressions.

I'm trying to think about use cases where we're reparenting really aggressively. Maybe a snap-together builder game?

Overall I think that reparenting will be an extremely rare operation in practice, and we shouldn't be focused on optimizing the perf there other than incidentally.

issue_context.title: Improve incrementality of transform propagation updates for siblings
issue_context.body: As of #4608 (for legitimate correctness reasons), adding or removing any child now results in recomputing the transform hierarchy for _every_ sibling. This is extremely suboptimal for large scenes. For example, despawning a single "house" entity in a scene with thousands of houses should not recompute the transform for every house (and the things inside of it). Given that transform propagation is often a bottleneck, fixing this should be a priority.
comments: Added to the 0.8 milestone; I agree that we should aim to get this fixed ASAP.

Apologies, I haven't quite followed the discussion on Github or Discord; but what was the proposed fix going to be since adding a marker component was seen as [untenable](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/3340#discussion_r786930527)?

Was it going to be the proposed [rfc](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/3329#issuecomment-1062160801)?

> what was the proposed fix going to be since adding a marker component was seen as https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/3340#discussion_r786930527?

If we can get better performance characteristics with a marker component, I'm alright with that as a stop-gap. 

If we can get either the scheduling changes or a [hierarchy redesign](https://github.com/bevyengine/rfcs/pull/53) in in time for  the next release, I'd prefer a more elegant and robust approach instead.
@cart @james7132, this is in the milestone. Is this still relevant following #4197?
Definitely still an issue. Any change to Children leads to propagating through the entire subtree.

This won't be solved / reviewed in time for 0.8. But should be prioritized / not forgotten. For now I'm adding a P-High so we don't lose it. We should also add this to the 0.9 milestone when that is created.

Spurious thought: since `Children`/`Parent`s are changed in tandem when applying hierarchy changes, and child order doesn't really matter. Shouldn't we be checking for `Changed<Parent>` instead of `Changed<Children>`? It'd be localized only to only the children which has a changed parent instead of all children of a parent with one or more changed children.
